text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein says Middle East peace talks reach criticial point. "We are in front of a dangerous turning point. I hope there will be a change in the picture and the peace process will be more serious and focused."
- Prime Minister Kabariti tells Rotary Club that Jordan is working for implementation of peace process.
- Opposition members of parliament say they oppose appointment of house speaker by acclaim.
- King says the Middle East is passing through its most dangerous stage. All peace lovers must join efforts to get out of this tunnel.
- Kabariti says king is ringing the alarm bells to get peace back on track.
- Jordanian ambassador in Israel meets Prime Minister Netanyahu's adviser Dore Gold.
- Opposition studies legal case against the government over weekly television programme which insults some members of parliament.
- King says Washington summit came at the right time, and that Netanyahu promised a "pleasant surprise".
- Kabariti reaffirms commitment to private sector, promises to address industry snags. Tells Amman Chamber of Industries that government will listen to industrialists' complaints.
- King says Jordan is waiting for a quick solution to the delayed Israeli pull-out from Hebron.
